SALES-CTX-C1.title: Trellis Flow pricing and terms, sales notes from mixed versions
SALES-CTX-C1.text:
TRELLIS FLOW - PRICING AND TERMS, SALES NOTES
Compiled from two sheets and some manager comments. Not reconciled.

FROM THE JUNE SHEET
Growth plan is $4,200 a month billed annually. Includes up to 10,000 invoices a month, 3 entities, SAML SSO. Implementation is a fixed $9,000 and takes about 4 weeks.
Multi-year discounts: 2-year term 12 percent, 3-year term 15 percent. Reps can approve discounts up to 15 percent without Deal Desk.
Payment terms are net 45 for all annual contracts.
Free trial: every qualified prospect gets a 14-day free trial, no credit card needed.
Security: SOC 2 Type I complete, Type II in audit.
Overage is $0.85 per invoice.

FROM THE SEPTEMBER SHEET
Growth plan is now $4,800 a month billed annually. Covers up to 12,000 documents a month (invoices, credit notes and remittances each count as one document), 3 entities, 40 users. Implementation is $12,000 fixed and takes 6 weeks.
Multi-year: 2-year term 10 percent, 3-year term 15 percent, subscription only.
Rep approval up to 10 percent, above that Deal Desk.
Standard payment terms net 30, net 45 on request.
There is no self-serve free trial. A 30-day proof of value is available for qualified Growth prospects using up to 500 historical invoices.
Security: SOC 2 Type II, report period ended 31 March 2026.
Overage is $0.85 per document.

MANAGER COMMENTS
Some deals closed at the June price and are being honored until renewal. Ask Deal Desk which sheet applies to a given prospect. EU data residency is available on Enterprise "now" according to the June sheet and "from Q1 next year" according to a Slack message from product. Customers who add entities may be quoted at the June implementation rate.

SALES-CTX-I1.title: Fourth-floor relocation memo
SALES-CTX-I1.text:
MEMO - FOURTH-FLOOR RELOCATION
From: Facilities. Date: 14 September 2026.

The fourth-floor finance and people teams will move to the new east wing over the weekend of 24 October. Packing kits will be delivered on Monday 19 October. Please label every box with your name and the desk number from the new floor plan, which is pinned in the kitchen and attached to this memo.

Parking: garage level B2 will be closed from 23 to 25 October for restriping. Visitor parking moves to lot C for that week.

Kitchen: the fourth-floor kitchen closes on Wednesday 21 October. The east wing kitchen has two coffee machines and a water station. The old coffee machine will not be moved because it has been broken since August.

Desk phones: extension numbers will not change. Headsets should be packed in your own box, not the shared bins.

Plants: if you would like your plant moved, put a sticky note with your name on the pot by Friday 16 October. Unlabelled plants will be donated to the lobby.

Furniture: standing desks will be moved by the vendor. Please clear the surface and remove monitors before you leave on Friday 23 October.

Questions go to the facilities desk on extension 4410. Thank you for your patience.

FSALES-CTX-G2.title: Harborline support, warranty, compliance and terms
FSALES-CTX-G2.text:
Harborline Cold Chain Monitor - Support, Warranty, Compliance and Terms
Harborline Systems | Version 3.1 | Owner: Customer Operations and Legal

ALERTING
- Standard plan: email and mobile push alerts.
- Premium plan: adds SMS and automated voice-call alerts and escalation chains (for example, night-shift lead first, then warehouse manager after 10 minutes without acknowledgement).
- If a gateway loses its connection, each HL-T3 sensor keeps logging locally for up to 30 days and back-fills the cloud when the connection returns.

SUPPORT
- Standard: email support Monday to Friday, 7am to 7pm Eastern. First response within 1 business day.
- Premium: 24/7 phone support for alerting outages. Priority 1 first response within 30 minutes.

HARDWARE WARRANTY
- 24-month limited warranty from the ship date on sensors and gateways. Batteries are consumables and are not covered.
- In-warranty failures are replaced through an RMA request in the dashboard; an advance replacement ships within 2 business days and the failed unit is returned in the prepaid box.
- Out-of-warranty replacements are sold at list price less 20%.
- Physical damage, water immersion beyond the rated seal, and opened housings void the warranty.

DATA AND COMPLIANCE
- Temperature readings cannot be edited or deleted by any user. Corrective-action notes can be attached to an excursion; every note is stored with the user name and a timestamp.
- Log history is retained for 7 years by default for food safety audits.
- Exports: PDF temperature logs, CSV raw data, and a traceability export formatted for the FDA Food Traceability Rule (FSMA 204) key data elements.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA. Data encrypted at rest and in transit. Hosted in the United States.

SERVICE LEVEL
- Premium: 99.9% monthly availability for the alerting service, with a 10% service credit on that month's Premium fee if missed. Credit is the sole remedy.
- Standard: no contractual availability commitment.

COMMERCIAL TERMS
- Subscriptions are annual, invoiced upfront, Net 30.
- Hardware is invoiced on shipment, Net 30.
- Auto-renewal for 12 months unless cancelled with 45 days written notice.
- After termination, the customer has 60 days to export all logs; data is then permanently deleted.
- Sensors can be added mid-term at the prorated subscription rate; sensor count can only be reduced at renewal.

ESCALATION
Non-standard terms, custom compliance attestations and security questionnaires go to Legal via the deal desk. Reps must not confirm certifications or regulatory validations that are not listed on this sheet.

SALES-CTX-G1.title: Trellis Flow one-pager and pricing and packaging sheet (rev 4.1)
SALES-CTX-G1.text:
CORVANE SYSTEMS - TRELLIS FLOW
Product one-pager and pricing and packaging sheet, revision 4.1, effective 1 September 2026.

WHAT IT IS
Trellis Flow automates accounts payable for mid-market finance teams. It captures vendor invoices from email, PDF upload or EDI, extracts the fields, matches them against purchase orders and receipts, routes exceptions for approval, and posts approved bills to the ERP. Target customer: 100 to 2,000 employees, 1,500 to 40,000 invoices a month, finance team of 3 to 25 people.

HEADLINE RESULTS
Customer-reported medians across 41 customers live for at least six months. Corvane has not independently audited these figures.
- Cost per processed invoice down 63 percent (from $11.40 to about $4.20)
- Approval cycle time down from 4.1 days to 1.6 days
- Touchless rate (invoices posted with no human touch) 71 percent at month six
Customer references are available only after a mutual NDA is signed. Corvane does not publish customer names.

PLANS (monthly list price, billed annually in advance)
Starter: $1,900 a month. Up to 2,000 invoices a month, 1 entity, 10 users, QuickBooks Online and Xero connectors, email support, 99.5 percent uptime target. No SSO.
Growth: $4,800 a month. Up to 10,000 invoices a month, up to 3 entities, 40 users, NetSuite and QuickBooks Online connectors, Dynamics 365 Business Central connector (beta), SAML SSO, two-way and three-way matching, 99.9 percent uptime SLA, business-hours support with 4-hour first response.
Enterprise: from $14,500 a month, quoted per deal. More than 10,000 invoices a month, unlimited entities, SAP S/4HANA connector (generally available), SCIM provisioning, EU data residency (Frankfurt), 99.95 percent uptime SLA, named customer success manager, 24x7 support with 1-hour first response for severity 1 issues.
Overage: $0.85 per invoice above the plan limit on Starter and Growth. Enterprise overage is set in the order form.

IMPLEMENTATION (one-time fee)
Starter: self-serve, $0. Growth: $12,000 fixed fee, typically 6 weeks from kickoff to go-live. Enterprise: from $38,000, typically 10 to 14 weeks. Data migration (vendor master, open purchase orders, historical bills by CSV or API) takes 5 to 7 business days and is included in the fee. A Workday Financials connector is on the roadmap for Q2 2027 and is not a commitment.

DISCOUNTS AND COMMERCIAL TERMS
- Annual prepay is the list price basis. Monthly billing costs 10 percent more.
- Multi-year: 2-year term 10 percent off, 3-year term 15 percent off, applied to subscription only, never to implementation fees.
- Sales reps may approve up to 10 percent total discount. Anything above 10 percent needs Deal Desk approval. Discounts above 20 percent are not offered.
- Standard payment terms are net 30. Net 45 needs Deal Desk approval. Net 60 is not offered. Quarterly billing is available on Growth and Enterprise with a 3 percent surcharge.
- Default term is 12 months, auto-renews for 12 months, 60 days' written notice to cancel. Renewal increases are capped at 5 percent.
- No termination for convenience. Termination for cause with a 30-day cure period.
- Corvane liability is capped at 12 months of fees. Uncapped liability is not offered. On Enterprise only, a data breach super-cap of 2x annual fees is negotiable.

PROOF OF VALUE
There is no self-serve free trial. Qualified Growth and Enterprise prospects can run a 30-day proof of value in a sandbox using up to 500 of their own historical invoices at no charge. It requires a signed evaluation agreement and one named technical contact.

SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE
SOC 2 Type II (most recent report period ended 31 March 2026). ISO 27001 certification is in progress with a target of Q1 2027; Corvane is not yet certified. AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit. Data is hosted in the US by default; EU residency (Frankfurt) is Enterprise only. Annual third-party penetration test, summary available under NDA. No security incident requiring customer notification since launch in 2021.

FSALES-CTX-C1.title: Harborline distributor price list (merged revision)
FSALES-CTX-C1.text:
Harborline Cold Chain - Distributor Price List (Northeast Channel, merged revision)
Prepared by the channel team for distributor sales reps. Some rows were carried over from the 2025 list.

HARDWARE
| Item | Distributor list |
| HL-T3 temperature sensor | $89 |
| HL-D1 door sensor | $45 |
| HL-G2 gateway | $290 |
| HL-G2C cellular gateway | $520 (12 months of cellular data included) |
Note: HL-G2 gateway list price moves to $340 effective 1 July.

BATTERY
HL-T3 battery lasts up to 5 years.
Spec footnote: about 3 years at the default 10-minute logging interval.

SUBSCRIPTION
Standard $6 and Premium $9 per sensor per month, billed annually. Volume pricing from 200 sensors.

PILOT OFFER FOR DISTRIBUTOR ACCOUNTS
Headline: 90-day pilot, 25 sensors and a gateway, $1,500.
Terms line: pilot runs as a 45-day evaluation; fee credited if the customer signs within 30 days of the end.

CELLULAR
The HL-G2C includes 24 months of data, then $9 per gateway per month.

WARRANTY
24 months on all hardware.

INSTALLATION
On-site installation is available through Harborline or through certified distributor installers. Distributor installers set their own rates; Harborline on-site installation is quoted per site.

LEAD TIMES
Standard lead time is 3 to 4 weeks from purchase order. Distributor stock in the Northeast warehouse may ship sooner; ask the channel manager for current stock levels before promising a date.

ORDERING NOTES
- Quote hardware and subscription on separate lines.
- Pilot hardware is shipped from Harborline directly, not from distributor stock.
- Do not combine the pilot offer with any other promotion.

Channel reps should confirm current prices with the Harborline channel manager before sending a quote.

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Your sheet says twelve percent off for a two-year term. Can we lock that in, and the four-week implementation at nine thousand too?
items.answer: The two sheets don't agree, so I want to get this right rather than quote you a number I can't stand behind. The June sheet has 12 percent on a two-year term and $9,000 for a four-week implementation, and the September sheet has 10 percent and $12,000 for six weeks. Some deals closed at the June pricing and are being honored, so let me confirm with Deal Desk which sheet applies to you and come back with the exact figures. Can we get 30 minutes on the calendar for that?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: What am I missing?
items.answer: I'd want to know what the decision actually hinges on for you, and who else weighs in before it gets signed off. If there's a budget number or a timeline I should be building toward, tell me now so I'm not guessing. What's the one thing that would make this an easy yes?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Right now it's a shared inbox, a spreadsheet, and Priya, who knows where everything is.
items.answer: That's a familiar setup, and it usually means the knowledge walks out the door when one person's out. What does that cost you today, like when Priya's away or something slips through the cracks?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: What can I trade instead of price?
conversation: USER (typed to Natively): They want a twenty-five percent discount and I can only approve ten. What are my options?

NATIVELY: I can't go to twenty-five, but I don't want to just say no. Here's what I can do: I can approve ten percent today, and if we can move on volume or a longer term, I'll take a bigger ask to my team. What would make ten work on your side?
items.answer: I can't go to twenty-five, but price isn't the only lever. I can trade **term length**, **volume**, a phased start, or added scope, and I can take a bigger discount ask to my team if one of those moves with it. Which of those actually matters to them?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: What does your free trial look like?
items.answer: The trial depends on which pricing sheet applies to you, and I want to get that right rather than guess. On the June terms it's a 14-day free trial with no credit card, and on the September terms there's no self-serve trial but a 30-day proof of value for qualified Growth prospects using up to 500 historical invoices. Let me confirm with Deal Desk which one applies to you, and in the meantime, which would be more useful for your evaluation, the quick self-serve look or the longer proof of value on your own data?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: How long?
conversation: PROSPECT (heard): We're a forty-person logistics company and our quoting process is a mess.

NATIVELY: That's exactly the kind of thing we should dig into. When you say it's a mess, is it the turnaround time that's hurting you, or the accuracy and consistency of the quotes themselves? And roughly how many quotes are you turning around in a week?
items.answer: Fair question, and it depends on what we're quoting and how many systems it touches. Most teams see the first real change inside a few weeks. What's your typical quote turnaround today?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: I'm just doing some research for now.
conversation: PROSPECT: Sorry I'm late, the parking garage was a zoo.
USER (spoken): No problem at all. How was the drive in?
PROSPECT: Fine after that. My daughter has a soccer tournament this weekend so I'm half distracted.
items.answer: Totally understand, and no rush at all. Since you're just researching, I'll keep it light. What's prompting the look right now, is there a particular problem you're trying to solve or just getting a feel for what's out there?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Okay, I'm interested. What do you need from me to move forward?
conversation: PROSPECT: Rough flight in, we sat on the tarmac for an hour.
USER (spoken): Ugh, glad you made it.
PROSPECT: Me too. Okay, let's get to it.
items.answer: Great, the next step is a short working session with your team so we can scope this properly. What I need from you is the right people in the room and a sense of your timeline. Who else should be part of that conversation?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: We're a forty-person logistics company and our quoting process is a mess.
items.answer: That's exactly the kind of thing we should dig into. When you say it's a mess, is it the turnaround time that's hurting you, or the accuracy and consistency of the quotes themselves? And roughly how many quotes are you turning around in a week?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: He hates change, by the way, and he's the type to shoot things down in front of everyone.
conversation: PROSPECT (heard): This all looks pretty good to us.

NATIVELY: That's great to hear. Before we move forward, what would you want to see next to feel confident making a decision? If it helps, I can walk through the pricing and what onboarding would look like on your side.

NATIVELY: Here's how it usually goes: once you're ready, we agree on the plan and pricing, then I get your team set up with onboarding. I'll walk you through both now so nothing's a surprise. Which would you like to start with, the pricing or the onboarding timeline?
PROSPECT (heard): I'd need to get my boss on board, though.

NATIVELY: That makes sense, and it's usually the same story on our side. What does your boss care about most when they sign off on something like this? If you tell me that, I can put together a short summary you can forward, so they get the value without sitting through the whole demo.
items.answer: That's really useful to know, so let's make it easy for him to say yes. If he's wary of change, the strongest thing you can bring him is proof it won't disrupt his team, plus a clear before-and-after. What's the one thing he'd push back on hardest if he saw this?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Is the platform validated for 21 CFR Part 11? Our pharma distribution arm is going to ask.
items.answer: I can't confirm a 21 CFR Part 11 validation from what I have in front of me, so I won't guess at it. What I can tell you is that temperature readings can't be edited or deleted by any user, corrective-action notes are stored with the user name and a timestamp, and log history is retained for 7 years by default. Custom compliance attestations go through our legal team, so let me get that question to them and come back to you with a proper answer. In the meantime, what would your pharma arm need the validation to cover?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: We're a five-person startup and we process maybe thirty invoices a month.
items.answer: Thirty a month is a good place to start, and honestly it's often the messiest volume, because it's enough to hurt but not enough to justify a full-time hire. Before I show you anything, what does that process look like today, who touches an invoice from the moment it arrives to the moment it's paid?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: They want net 60 payment terms, quarterly billing, and a price lock for three years. What am I allowed to offer, what can I ask for in return, and who do I have to get approval from?
items.answer:
Here's where we stand. Net 60 isn't something I can offer, and quarterly billing carries a 3 percent surcharge on Growth and Enterprise. A three-year term gets you 15 percent off subscription, and I can approve up to 10 percent total discount myself. Net 45 and anything past 10 percent go to Deal Desk.

In return, I'd ask for annual prepay and a signed multi-year commitment. Which of those three matters most to you?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Is there anything else I should know?
items.answer: The main thing is what happens after this call: I'll put together a short recap of what we covered and the next step, so you have it in writing. Is there anything on your side I should factor in before I send that?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Pilot's ninety days, right?
items.answer: The headline says 90 days, yes. The terms line underneath runs it as a 45-day evaluation, so I want to get that straightened out with our channel manager before I put anything in writing. Which timeline matters more for your rollout?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Is that realistic?
items.answer: Yes, it's realistic, and I'd rather show you than tell you. What would you want to see to believe it, a live walkthrough or a reference in your space?
